summary.headline: Cemindia FY26 revenue crossed INR10,000 crore (INR10,061 crore, +9%) and Q4 EBITDA margin hit 15.1%, helped by one-time claims and provision releases.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating income rose to INR2,973 crore for the full year and Q4 EBITDA jumped 66% YoY to INR450 crore at a 15.1% margin. Management attributed the margin spike to one-time items: INR150 crore of claims realised (INR100 crore in Q4, partly booked as other income) and release of provisions held for metro jobs now completed. Management guided that the normal EBITDA margin is about 10-10.5%. Order book stands at INR29,000 crore, including L1 positions of about INR1,600 crore and an April win of about INR3,200 crore. FY27 guidance is revenue growth of at least 20-25%, with an order-inflow target of about INR25,000 crore.

segments.name: Group / captive EPC (Adani-linked) and data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre is a new division with 3-4 jobs secured from the group; cumulative data centre order book about INR3,000 crore. Management is keeping it within the group for now, with Vizag opportunities mentioned.

segments.name: Metro and tunnelling
segments.commentary: Bangalore and Mumbai metro jobs completed and contributed to Q4 margin. Chennai Metro has about 40% of value left, with completion expected around end-2027 to early 2028; the company owns 4 TBMs at Chennai and sold a Bangalore TBM. Tunnelling market (metro, road and other) is cited at about INR1 lakh crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue to grow at least 25% per MD's opening answer; later answers say 20-25% is quite possible on top line.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR25,000 crore, against about INR19,000 crore secured in FY26 (including L1 and April wins).
Sustainable EBITDA margin excluding other income guided at about 10-10.5%; management says it will try for more than 10%.
FY27 capex planned at INR350-400 crore, against INR260 crore in FY26.
PAT margin: management aims to maintain the same momentum and margin.
Dividend was supposed to be declared but is delayed; management said it will be declared within a few weeks.
Revenue growth of 20-25% a year for up to about 3 years was stated as the aspiration; no fundraising planned.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at INR350-400 crore versus INR260 crore in FY26.
Chennai Metro TBMs have completed breakthrough; about 40% of value left, completion expected around end-2027 to early 2028 (stations included in scope).
New TBMs being bought for Pune Metro and Delhi Metro; large-diameter TBM would be needed for large diameter tunnel work.
No idle TBMs at present; a TBM is typically engaged for 3-4 years on a job.
demand_pricing: Work in hand (order book) stands at INR29,000 crore versus about INR20,000-21,000 crore a year earlier; management says no legacy jobs remain.
FY26 order wins about INR14,000 crore excluding L1 and April wins; with L1 and April wins, about INR19,000 crore versus about INR7,000 crore in prior years.
Pipeline of about INR70,000 crore, of which group is about 35-40%; roads and highways and tunnelling are the main segments, each about INR1 lakh crore market.

Vadhvan port: breakwater tender and dredging and reclamation tender out; company is L1 for the breakwater job and progress has stalled since technical bid opening in October with customer reasons unknown.
Mor Sagar (JV with group, 27% stake) is at early design stage; EPC award could go to the company or another party based on price.

Around 30% of jobs have fixed-price (star price) arrangements with commodity pass-through in both directions; about 80% of jobs have a clause protecting against normal inflation but not abnormal war-driven cost spikes.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin expansion to about 12% excluding other income, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited completed metro jobs, claims realised and release of provisions kept for metro jobs; it said this is not a regular phenomenon and guided 10-10.5% going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 margin came from claims?
qa_highlights.answer: INR150 crore of claims were realised for the full year, of which INR100 crore in Q4; part was booked in other income (mainly interest) and part in revenue. The claim was described as one-time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mobilisation advance and how much is interest-bearing?
qa_highlights.answer: Mobilisation advance was INR1,400 crore at March 2026, with about 90% interest-free and about 10% interest-bearing; interest terms depend on the project and the promoter-group's contract with the client.

qa_highlights.question: How is the data centre business progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: A new division has 3-4 group jobs and about INR3,000 crore of data centre orders; the focus is on group opportunities for now, with Vizag opportunities mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Adani road-tunnel project and Vadhvan?
qa_highlights.answer: The group is L1 on the road tunnel job but has not yet received the order; the company will bid if it is awarded. Vadhvan is a slow-moving project and the company is waiting on customer decisions on the breakwater and dredging tenders.

qa_highlights.question: How much inflation risk is passed through to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% of jobs are fixed-price with commodity pass-through, about 80% have normal-inflation escalation clauses, and the remainder has no protection; management expects some margin impact that will be priced into future bids.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a dividend and fundraising plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The dividend was not declared this year due to a process delay and management said it will be declared within a few weeks. No fundraising is planned as the company has adequate funds.

risks_watch: Q4 margin of 15.1% included one-time claims and provision releases; normalised margin guided at about 10-10.5%, so Q1 FY27 margin is a key test.
Vadhvan port project is slow-moving with no clarity on the timing of the customer's release of the breakwater work.
Commodity and fuel inflation (crude, cement, steel) could squeeze margins on the about 70% of jobs without full pass-through, and this is not yet quantified.
Payment risk from some state governments; management says central government payments are fine but several states have weak treasuries and some bills remain uncertified.
Dependence on group orders: group is 35-40% of the INR70,000 crore pipeline; the road-tunnel award to the group is pending.
Management could not give Bangladesh receivables or the Q1 FY27 order details beyond L1 and April wins; the call reported the Bangladesh receivables as under control.
Dividend declaration pending; the company said it will be declared within a few weeks.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 scale, profit and order intake, but guarded on the sustainability of Q4 margin, which management stated was not a recurring trend. Answers were often vague or deferred on the timing of tenders, the Vadhvan delays and the state payment environment.
key_quotes: Revenue should be at least 25% more than this year.
But this will not be a regular phenomenon. It will be around 10% to 10.5% going forward.
Interest-bearing is, I think, around 10% of the total advances as of now.
